themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the system often changes itself while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers are called non-deterministic with no fixed baseline, identity resolution lacks any verified set of who is really the same person, incrementality tests get reshaped by the platform being tested, content review has no stable standard reviewers agree on, and ad supply integrity work notes that fraud and real performance both look like numbers going up.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three models say agents gain by looking human and propose fast lanes and perks for declaring, journey orchestration keeps failing because channel owners are paid on their own numbers, the semantic context layer is called a political settlement rather than a data model, and ad supply integrity is described as a market financially attached to fake volume.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Today all three models again answer safe agent execution with a single gateway or proxy that caps spend, rate, and audience size and strips credentials from agents, while the consent problem gets one checkpoint over every data exit and journey orchestration gets one shared contact log that can say no.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The consent and deletion answers say proof dies at the edge of black-box ad platforms and already-trained models, safe agent execution notes vendors expose no rollback or agent identity, incrementality says platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and the ad supply answers shift judgment to the advertiser's own sales records.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers converge on an approved-claims library that limits what the model may say because implied claims from tone and combination cannot be checked, and the semantic context layer answers accept that teams legitimately need different definitions of customer and settle for forcing disclosure of which one was used.
